chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaaz, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saw the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth, he turned and saw a man committing adultery, so he supplicated against him and he died. Then he saw another, supplicated against him, and he died, until he saw a third, supplicated against them, and they died.

So Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, Revealed unto him: 'O Ibrahim! Indeed, your supplication is answered, so do not supplicate against My servants, for if I willed, I would not have created them. I created My creation in three categories: A servant who worships Me and does not associate anything with Me, so I reward him; and a servant who worships other than Me, so he will not escape Me; and a servant who worships other than Me, so I will bring out from his loins one who worships Me.'

Then he turned and saw a carcass on the coast of the sea, half of it in the water and half on the land. The beasts of the sea came and ate what was in the water, then returned, and some of them pounced on others and ate each other. The beasts of the land came and ate from it, and some of them pounced on others and ate each other.
At that, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was astonished at what he saw and said: 'My Lord, show me how You bring back the dead.'
He said: 'How do You bring back that which has consumed each other?' He said: 'Have you no faith?' He said: 'Yes, but just to reassure my heart.'

Meaning, until he sees this just as he sees all things. He said: 'Take four birds, draw them to you, then place a portion of them on each mountain, cut them up, and mix them up just as this carcass was mixed up among these beasts that ate each other.'
So he mixed them, then placed a portion of them on each mountain, then called them, and they came to him hastening. When he called them, they responded, and the mountains were ten in number.
ai.seo_question: How did Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) demonstrate the resurrection of the dead according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this narrative from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'Istidraj' and the three categories of creation, highlighting Ibrahim’s transition from intellectual certainty to experiential tranquility (li-yatma'inna qalbi). The miracle of the four birds serves as a tangible proof of resurrection, paralleling the Quranic account where Allah demonstrates power over disintegrated matter to affirm the ease of reassembly for the Creator.
